mekayis.metin: (ضَمَّ) الضَّادُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مُلَاءَمَةٍ بَيْنَ شَيْئَيْنِ. يُقَالُ: ضَمَمْتُ الشَّيْءَ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ فَأَنَا أَضُمُّهُ ضَمًّا. وَهَذِهِ إِضْمَامَةٌ مِنْ خَيْلٍ، أَيْ جَمَاعَةٌ. وَفَرَسٌ سَبَّاقُ الْأَضَامِيمِ، أَيِ الْجَمَاعَاتِ. وَإِضْمَامَةٌ مِنْ كُتُبٍ مِثْلُ إِضْبَارَةٍ. وَمِنَ الْبَابِ: أَسَدٌ ضَمْضَمٌ وَضَمَاضِمٌ: يَضُمُّ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ.

g: to be put together, to be gathered, to be collected, to be contracted
to be joined, be associated, be annexed

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: ضَمَّ • (ḍamma) I (non-past يَضُمُّ (yaḍummu), verbal noun ضَمّ (ḍamm))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Form I verb from the root ض م م (ḍ m m).
g: to gather, hoard, join, bring near
to mark or pronounce with damma
verbal noun of ضَمَّ (ḍamma, “to gather”) (form I)
the sound of short /u/, indicated in writing by a damma

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Instance noun of the Form I verb ضَمَّ (ḍamma, “to embrace; to gather; to compress the lips”), from the root ض م م (ḍ m m). When used to describe the vowel ـُ (u), ضَمَّة (ḍamma) means “an instance of [lip-]rounding”, since u is the only short vowel in Arabic that is pronounced with lip-rounding.
g: a number of horses assembled from every quarter for a race
damma, ḍamma, the diacritic in the Arabic script that represents the vowel /u/, appearing as a small curl placed above a letter: ـُ
